SnapLogic Named One of Network World’s “Ten Open Source Companies to Watch”
SaaS Integration Pioneer Recognized for Open Source Data Integration Framework
Summarize this with AI
 ChatGPT
 Claude.AI
SAN MATEO, Calif. – Sep 4, 2008 – SnapLogic, Inc., the SaaS integration company, today announced that IDG’s Network World, a leading provider of news, analysis, reviews, events, and education on information technology, has selected SnapLogic as one of Network World’s Ten Open Source Companies to Watch. Network World’s Ten Open Source Companies to Watch highlights ten companies that are developing open source technologies to make computing faster, smarter, and more affordable for corporate users. SnapLogic enables enterprises to integrate data on both sides of the enterprise firewall and to create custom integration solutions, including integrations with both SaaS and non-SaaS applications, enterprise mashups, and rich Internet applications (RIAs). To learn more about SnapLogic, visit www.snaplogic.com.
“Software as a Service is one of the most important trends in enterprise IT today. SnapLogic enables organizations to realize the full benefit of their SaaS investments by quickly and easily integrating SaaS data with other data in the cloud and data behind the firewall. Simply put, we make it easy for organizations to integrate SaaS application with the rest of their business IT infrastructure,” said Chris Marino, chief executive officer, SnapLogic. “We’re thrilled that our pioneering work in this important area has been recognized by the editors of Network World.”
In naming SnapLogic and other companies to its list of open source companies to watch, Network World noted that the honorees have distinguished themselves by creating “intelligent, cutting-edge technologies with an eye on making computing faster, smarter, and cheaper for corporate users.” The feature also indicated that open source is “no longer just a trendy conversation,” and that “the decision is no longer a question of open source, but about what product is best at solving computing problems regardless of how it was built.”

SnapLogic brings SaaS integration to the enterprise.
